title: What If You Jumped Into a Hole Through the Earth?
description:
Gus dug a hole straight through the planet and jumped in. This is what physics says happens next.

The numbers, for an airless tunnel through the centre of the real Earth:
• One way: 38 minutes 11 seconds
• Top speed at the centre: about 22,000 mph (35,700 km/h)
• Round trip: 76 minutes. Forever.
(The famous "42 minutes" assumes the Earth has the same density all the way through. With the real, denser core it is 38.)

Sources:
• A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", American Journal of Physics 83, 231 (2015)
• PREM Earth model: Dziewonski & Anderson, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 25, 297 (1981)
• Core temperature: Anzellini et al., Science 340, 464 (2013). Sun's surface: NASA Sun Fact Sheet

Every number is computed in code and checked. Animation, narration and music are made with software and AI tools.
